title: A simultaneous subterminal site presentation and its module equivalences
statement: Let $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal S)$ be a Grothendieck topos presented on a small site $\mathcal S$ [def-weil-pbc-topos], let $R$ be a commutative ring object, and let $U,V\hookrightarrow1$ be subterminal objects with $U\cup V=1$; put $W=U\times V$. There is a full subcategory $\mathcal E\subset\mathcal T$ with a set of objects, closed under finite limits and containing the sheafified representables of $\mathcal S$ and $1,U,V,W$, with a small subcanonical site structure whose covers are the jointly epimorphic families (up to choice of a set of representatives). In particular $\{C\times U,C\times V\}\to C$ is a cover for every $C\in\mathcal E$. The nerve $N(F)(C)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(C,F)$ is an equivalence $\mathcal T\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E)$ carrying every object of $\mathcal E$ to its represented sheaf. For $Z=1,U,V,W$ it identifies $\mathcal T/Z$ with $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E/Z)$ for the localized topology [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and carries the restricted ring $R_Z$ to $N(R)|_Z$. These equivalences induce additive exact equivalences of the categories of module sheaves over these rings [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and triangulated equivalences of their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. They commute with restriction and its composition comparisons; hence their identifications of left and right adjoints preserve the adjunction units, counits, and nested-localization adjunction mates.

source.place: Tag 03A1 (lemma-special-equivalence); finite-limit closure with prescribed subterminals and transport of internal rings, modules and localized slices are the agent extension of this comparison lemma.

proof.text: Work in the coefficient universe of the given small-site presentation. The original site need not have pullbacks. Apply [lem-trf-sieve-sheaves-covering-site] to choose a covering-family site $\mathcal A$ and an equivalence $H:\mathcal T\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal A)$, with inverse $K$. If the original site already has this form, use the identity. Sheafified representables of the original site exist by [lem-trf-sieve-set-sheafification-exists]. In $\mathcal T$ start with the set consisting of those objects, $1,U,V,W$, and the objects $K(h_a^\#)$ for $a\in\mathcal A$. Including this last set will let us apply the covering-site comparison without imposing extra assumptions on the original site.

source.place: Tags 00ZM (proposition-sheafification-adjoint-topology), 03CI (lemma-topos-good-site); covering-site replacement is the cited agent generalization.

proof.text: Let $E_0$ be the preceding set. Given $E_n$, adjoin a chosen terminal object and one chosen pullback for every cospan between its objects to obtain $E_{n+1}$; retain $E_n$. These limits exist: sheaf limits on $\mathcal A$ are computed sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise], and their universal properties transport through $H,K$. Each stage is a set because the previous object set and all its Hom sets are sets. Put $E=\bigcup_{n\geq0}E_n$ and take the full subcategory $\mathcal E$ on it. A cospan uses finitely many objects, all in some common stage, so its chosen pullback lies in the next stage. Thus $\mathcal E$ has a terminal object and pullbacks computed in $\mathcal T$, hence all finite limits (products are pullbacks over $1$ and equalizers are pullbacks of diagonals). The inclusion, and therefore $F=H|_{\mathcal E}$, preserve these limits. This constructs the required single closure, rather than making unrelated choices of sites for $U,V,W$.

source.place: Tag 03CI (lemma-topos-good-site), inductive closure construction, with only terminal objects and pullbacks needed here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-of-sheaf-generators] to the small covering site $\mathcal A$ and the fully faithful finite-limit-preserving $F:\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal A)$. Its generator hypothesis holds because $K(h_a^\#)\in E_0$ and $HK(h_a^\#)\cong h_a^\#$. We obtain the epimorphic covering precoverage on $\mathcal E$ and a sheaf equivalence with underlying nerve $X\mapsto(C\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(H C,X))$. Compose with $H$ and use its fully faithful Hom bijections: the resulting functor is naturally $N(B)(C)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(C,B)$. Replace the equivalence functor along this natural isomorphism to use exactly $N$. Since $\mathcal E$ is full, $N(C)=h_C$ for $C\in\mathcal E$; thus every represented presheaf is a sheaf and the topology is subcanonical. Joint epimorphy is unchanged by $H$ (its Hom bijections preserve and reflect right cancellation), so the covers are exactly the jointly epimorphic families in $\mathcal T$.

source.place: Tag 03A1 (lemma-special-equivalence), clauses (1)-(5); use the existing fully faithful generator formulation.

proof.text: We check the binary families are jointly epimorphic. For subterminal sheaves, their join is the local closure of their pointwise union: a section belongs to it if its restrictions locally belong to one of the two subsheaves. This description is a sheaf by the transitivity axiom for coverings and gluing; it is the least subsheaf containing both because any such subsheaf contains these local gluings. Consequently $U\cup V=1$ means that locally on the original site the unique terminal section lifts to $U$ or $V$. If $a,b:C\to B$ agree after both projections $C\times U\to C$ and $C\times V\to C$, restrict any section of $C$ to such a cover. There it lifts to one of the two products and its images under $a,b$ agree. The separatedness axiom then gives $a=b$. Hence each binary family covers for the precoverage just constructed; both product objects belong to $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Tag 03A1 (lemma-special-equivalence), epimorphic-family topology; direct verification using the sheaf and topology axioms.

proof.text: Select covering-family representatives using [lem-weil-pbc-small-set-of-covering-families], with the prescribed set $\operatorname{Cov}_0$ consisting of all these binary covers, indexed by the set $E$. The covering-class axioms hold by the precoverage of step 3; its pullbacks exist by step 2. Thus the representatives can retain every displayed binary family while preserving the site axioms, and every jointly epimorphic family is combinatorially equivalent to a chosen covering. The generated topology, its sheaves, and $N$ do not change.

source.place: Tag 000X (lemma-coverings-site), retaining a prescribed set of coverings.

proof.text:
For each $Z=1,U,V,W$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable] to the subcanonical site $\mathcal E$ and its object $Z$. Compose the equivalence $\mathcal T/Z\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E)/h_Z$ induced by $N$ with its fibre equivalence to $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal E/Z)$; here $h_Z=h_Z^\#$ by subcanonicity. Explicitly it sends $p:B\to Z$ to
$$N_Z(B,p)(C\xrightarrow c Z)=\{b:C\to B\mid p b=c\}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T/Z}((C,c),(B,p)).$$
Restriction along arrows of $\mathcal E/Z$ is precomposition. This is the localized topology in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and makes the choice of each slice comparison explicit.

For an arrow $t:Z'\to Z$ among these objects and $(B\xrightarrow p Z)$, the comparison with slice restriction is the bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T/Z'}((C,c'),(B\times_Z Z',\operatorname{pr}_2))\longrightarrow\{b:C\to B\mid p b=t c'\},\qquad(b,c')\longmapsto b.$$
Its inverse is $b\mapsto(b,c')$. For $Z\to1$ this says $N_Z(B\times Z\to Z)=N(B)|_Z$. For $Z''\xrightarrow s Z'\xrightarrow t Z$ both iterated and direct comparisons send a lift to its $B$ component. They therefore agree under the canonical pullback associator, and are identity comparisons for identity arrows. This proves compatibility with composition, including both $W\to U\to1$ and $W\to V\to1$. Applied to $R$, the same formula sends addition, multiplication, zero and one to those on the $R$ component, hence sends $R_Z=R\times Z\to Z$ to $N(R)|_Z$.

source.place: Tags 00Y1 and 04GZ, product/fibre calculation; relocalization comparison is Tag 03EH (lemma-relocalize).

proof.text: View the internal commutative ring $R$ as its section-ring sheaf using [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-ring-object-sectionwise-reconstruction]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-equivalence-ring-transport] to the equivalence whose direct functor is $N$. It gives the transported sheaf of rings with underlying sheaf $N(R)$ and invertible structural map $N^{-1}N(R)\to R$. The operations are exactly those obtained by applying $N$ to the ring operations and its product comparisons. In the Hom description they are the pointwise operations on maps to $R$. Apply the same construction to each explicit $N_Z$; by step 7 its coefficient sheaf is precisely $N(R)|_Z$. Thus we have ringed-topos equivalences, with invertible structural maps, on the whole topos and all four slices.

source.place: Tag 03CR (lemma-morphism-ringed-topoi-comes-from-morphism-ringed-sites), carry along the rings; sites.tex Proposition 00YV, ring objects as sextuples.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport] to these ringed equivalences, whose sites are small relative to the module universe and whose structural maps have just been shown invertible. It gives additive exact equivalences between the module-sheaf categories, both on the whole topos and the slices, and their termwise induced equivalences of ordinary unbounded derived categories. It also supplies commutation with further restrictions. For the slice-side module category, the concrete identification uses [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]: the restricted ring on the element site is $(A,z)\mapsto R(A)$ and restricted modules have $(j_Z^*M)(A,z)=M(A)$. This identifies internal slice modules with the module sheaves to which the transport lemma applies.

source.place: Tags 03CR, 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), 04IE and 04J4; the exact and derived equivalence refinement is the cited existing transport statement.

proof.text: The restriction comparisons of these module equivalences are the ones of step 7: on an internal module the underlying lift $(m,c')$ is sent to $m$, preserving sums and the scalar action because both are computed on this component. Thus the module squares satisfy the same identity and composition equations. They hold degreewise on complexes and hence after localization. The derived equivalences are triangulated: an additive equivalence preserves biproducts, negatives, and the cone matrix $\begin{pmatrix}d_L&f\\0&-d_K\end{pmatrix}$, as well as the shift differential $-d_K$; it therefore sends each cone triangle to the corresponding cone triangle. The characterization of distinguished triangles in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives the assertion in both directions, including unbounded complexes.

source.place: Definition 05RU (definition-derived-category), with the cone-triangle triangulation; sites-modules.tex Definition 04IX, sectionwise restriction.

proof.text: Choose the identifications of the restriction adjoints as their adjunction-compatible conjugates under the equivalences. A right-adjoint identification is uniquely counit-compatible by [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]; the left-adjoint identification is uniquely unit-compatible by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. The other adjunction transformation then agrees as well: its transpose is the identity, so injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection determines it. Thus both units and counits are preserved. Finally use the explicit mate formula in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]: the mate of $\alpha:L_2G\to HL_1$ is $(R_2H\varepsilon_1)\circ(R_2\alpha R_1)\circ(\eta_2GR_1)$. Under the comparison isomorphisms each of its three factors is the corresponding transported factor. Their composite is therefore the transported mate. Applying this to the composition comparisons verified in steps 7 and 10 proves preservation of the nested-localization mates; no inference from mere isomorphism of endpoints is used.

source.place: Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints); the mate formula is that recorded in def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate (sites-cohomology.tex Remark 07A7).

There are no new nodes and the statement is the same as the base (unsplit, no proof). The item came from the re-split of the parent lem-sp-ringed-topos-binary-descent; that note applies to the parent, not to this ordinary first split. The statement is true: it is 03CI/03A1 applied to the set {1,U,V,W} plus ring, module and derived transport. I tested U=1, V=0; U=V=1; W=0; the degenerate topos; and R=0. Step 3 meets every hypothesis of site-of-sheaf-generators: the nerve is Hom_T(C,-) by full faithfulness, which makes the topology subcanonical. Step 4 correctly shows the binary family is jointly epimorphic using the local closure of U∪V and separatedness. Step 5 uses Cov_0 = the binary families. Steps 6-7 give the explicit fibre formula and the pullback-bijection coherence, and send R_Z to N(R)|_Z. Steps 8-9 transport the ring with an invertible structural map, then the modules and derived categories, with the slice ring (U,s)↦R(U). Step 10 checks that cones and shifts are preserved. Step 11 identifies the adjoints by the unique counit- and unit-compatible conjugates, and the mates are preserved factor by factor. Their closures contain no trace-formula, Poincaré-duality or nt-assume nodes, so they lie outside both assumptions and I accept them.
